paper: MASS: Multi-agent simulation scaling for portfolio construction
headline_mechanism: MASS simulates 16 heterogeneous investor types with 32 agents each, aggregates their five-of-20 selections using learned type-distribution weights and alpha=0.5, optimizes the distribution with simulated annealing, and holds the highest signals.

source_anchors.claim: The system defines 16 investor types with 32 agents per type.
Each agent receives 20 candidate stocks and selects five.
Agent decisions are aggregated using an investor-type distribution and alpha equal to 0.5.
The distribution is optimized by simulated annealing with initial temperature 40 and 100 iterations.

preserved_elements: 20-stock candidate pools and five selections per agent
alpha=0.5 aggregation of learned distribution and shared base signal
cross-sectional ranking of aggregated agent decisions
approximated_elements: 16 distinct JKP characteristics replace LLM investor personas
deterministic cyclic candidate pools replace unreleased random pool assignments
characteristic ranks replace missing per-agent decisions
trailing type RankIC histories replace the paper's unavailable optimization data
monthly common deciles replace weekly top-20% holdings
invented_elements: mean-minus-covariance-risk annealing objective scale and cooling rate
common value-weighted long/short decile portfolio adapter
portfolio_adapter: The aggregated MASS score is ranked within the frozen monthly top-1,000 U.S. universe and mapped to common value-weighted long/short deciles with 10 bp one-way cost.
claim_boundary: This is a researcher-authored MASS-inspired heterogeneous-agent simulation, not the unavailable LLM decisions, paper pool assignments, learned distribution trajectory, weekly holdings, or native results.
